titleDv: ޤާނޫނު ނަންބަރު 13/2008 (އެންޓި-ކޮރަޕްޝަން ކޮމިޝަނުގެ ޤާނޫނު) އަށް ... ވަނަ އިސްލާހު ގެނައުމުގެ ބިލު
summary: This is a government bill, presented by the Felidhoo MP Adam Zahir, that amends the Anti-Corruption Commission Act (Act No. 13/2008). Under the current law, the Commission's members choose their own president and vice-president from among themselves and then inform the President and Parliament within 48 hours. The bill changes this so that the President of the Maldives sends Parliament one or more names from among the Commission's members, and appoints as president or vice-president a person approved by a majority of MPs present and voting. It also removes the rule that lets the Commission's members force their president or vice-president out of that post, and makes resignations from these posts go to the President instead of the Commission.
whyItMatters: The choice of who leads the Anti-Corruption Commission would move from the Commission's own members to the President of the Maldives, subject to approval by Parliament.
keyProvisions: Clause 1 rewrites Article 7: the President appoints the Commission's president and vice-president from among its members, after submitting one or more names to Parliament and getting a majority vote of the MPs present and voting.

Clause 2 deletes Article 10(c) and (d), which require the president or vice-president to resign that post if a majority of Commission members decide they are not doing the job properly, while keeping them on as ordinary members.
Clause 3 deletes Article 11(d), under which the Commission itself fills a vacant president or vice-president post within 72 hours.

Clause 4 rewrites Article 15(b): a president or vice-president who wants to resign from that post sends a letter to the President of the Maldives, and the post ends when the President receives it (currently the letter goes to the Commission or its president).
Clause 5 says the current president and vice-president stay in their posts until they leave office under the law.
Clause 6 says the law takes effect when it is passed, ratified and published in the Government Gazette.
whoIsAffected: The Anti-Corruption Commission's members, president and vice-president, the President of the Maldives, and Parliament.
statedReasons: The government says the bill is meant to strengthen how independent commissions are run and to make the method for appointing commission presidents and vice-presidents from among their members the same across commissions.
